To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the addition of new units (neurons) in a dictionary (network) can improve its performance, (2) the deletion of units can further improve performance, (3) both the addition and deletion are controlled by the performance of the dictionary (network), and (4) sparsity can be used to facilitate adaptation of connectivity in the dictionary

(i) the proposed approach can adapt to the nonstationary data and outperform fixed-size online dictionary learning, (ii) this is achieved by adding and removing dictionary elements and by introducing sparsity on the dictionary elements, and (iii) this is particularly useful when the input is sparse with nearly disjoint supports

the proposed neurogenesis-inspired dictionary-learning framework is a powerful tool for online representation learning in the nonstationary environments, and can outperform the existing methods by a considerable margin in the presence of such data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of learning a representation of the input in the presence of changing data distributions.
the design of a new online dictionary-learning framework that is capable of adapting to the changing environment and improving the performance of the model.

the design of online dictionary learning algorithms for non-stationary data, which can adapt their architecture to the data distribution, while preserving the advantages of dictionary-based models (such as interpretability and robustness to noise).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed approach is able to learn better dictionaries, in terms of both representation quality and dictionary size, than the fixed-size dictionary model of Mairal, Bach, Ponce, and Sapiro (2009) on the same datasets.
the proposed neurogenesis-inspired online dictionary learning approach can outperform the state of the art in nonstationary environments.
the neurogenesis-inspired dictionary learning approach can significantly improve the online sparse coding performance in the presence of changing data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a novel online sparse coding model which is capable of incorporating the addition and removal of dictionary elements (hidden units) and is capable of adapting to the nonstationary environment in an efficient way.
we have developed a novel online dictionary learning framework that can be used to model and learn representations in a changing world.

we have proposed a novel online sparse coding framework that can adapt its dictionary to the non-stationary environment, and that we have empirically demonstrated the effectiveness of this model in a variety of real-life and synthetic datasets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the online setting, the addition and deletion (birth and death) of hidden units is a natural way to adapt the representation to the changing world.
, when learning in non-staionary environments, the ability to dynamically adapt model’s architecture can lead to significant performance improvements.

the proposed neurogenesis-inspired dictionary learning approach can be used as a powerful tool for online representation learning in changing environments, where model architecture adaptation is crucial for performance.
